text:
ida: Bringing up Cytos7B today. Converter ran but runtime shows a token-stride off-by-one in KV cache; outputs diverge from upstream after ~1k tokens. Anyone seen this pattern?

sam: Sounds like a hidden BOS/sentinel from the tokenizer. Quick check: run tokenizer.encode('') and compare to HF tokenizer.

ida: Good call. Cytos tokenizer returns [0] for empty string, hf-cytos returns []. So theres a leading BOS.

marco: That would shift kv indices by 1. But watch out  some models use sentinel to anchor rotary phase, so stripping may move the divergence point.

ida: Ran convert with --preserve-bos; immediate drift gone but divergence now at ~2048 tokens instead of 1024. Maybe rotary_base/frequency mismatch.

sam: Try forcing runtime rotary_base=10000 and run per-head phase checks. Also run int4 quant path  quant can reveal subtle misalignments.

aya: I pushed a tiny conv option to optionally strip single-token BOS: https://git.redwood/conv/pulls/128 (WIP). Use only as stopgap.

infra-bot: CI job 9123 started on pool-gpu-small for compare-run.

ida: Next steps: run rotary_base=10000 trace, run quantized eval, open ML ticket with repro and logs. Thanks :thumbsup:
notes: short triage thread: hidden BOS caused KV offset; preserving BOS moved divergence implying rotary freq/base mismatch; next steps include forcing rotary_base and running int4 evals
